standard_prerequisites: The translation of a Turing machine M and input w into a first-order sentence T(M,w) describing the machine program, a halting sentence E(M,w), and the configuration formula C(M,w,n) describing the machine configuration after n steps, together with the notion of validity of a first-order sentence.
The configuration lemma of the same unit: for each n, if M has not halted after n steps, then T(M,w) entails C(M,w,n); published as corpus card X1-logic-tm-undec-config.

The halting-configuration lemma of the same unit: if the configuration formula describes a halting configuration (the state and scanned symbol pair has no applicable instruction), then C(M,w,k) entails E(M,w); published as corpus card X1-logic-olp-tm-halt-config-implies-halt.
core_obligations: Show that if M halts on input w, then T(M,w) implies E(M,w) is valid: let k be the halting step and m the scanned square; by the configuration lemma T(M,w) entails C(M,w,k), and C(M,w,k) contains as conjuncts the halting state and scanned-symbol atoms with no applicable instruction, which is exactly a halting configuration.
Apply the halting-configuration lemma to get C(M,w,k) entails E(M,w), compose with T(M,w) entails C(M,w,k), and conclude T(M,w) entails E(M,w), which is the validity of the implication.
proof_roadmap: Two-cited-lemma composition: halting fixes the halting step k and makes the configuration description at step k a halting configuration by the definition of the configuration formula's conjuncts; the configuration lemma lifts it to entailment by T(M,w); the halting-configuration lemma derives E(M,w); entailment transitivity gives the valid implication.
difficulty_reason: A composition of two proved lemmas with a definitional bridge (the configuration formula at the halting step contains the halting state and scanned symbol conjuncts); the argument direction and the entailment transitivity are the only care points.
